compiled_state.title: Bridge sync chronic-silence: close 4 silent-drop paths + round-trip coverage
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context
The Jira and DSO bridge silently drops events on every cron tick. Local STATUS, EDIT, and COMMENT mutations vanish whenever any other commit lands on the tracker branch between ticks (suggestion records, inbound bot CREATE commits, batched local mutations) — the outbound bridge HEAD~1..HEAD diff window with --depth=2 fetch can only see the most recent commit's added events. Jira-imported descriptions arrive as None because the inbound parser treats Jira REST v3 ADF JSON as a string. ESCALATED 4-agent investigation across jira-dig-1995, jira-dig-1604, and 92b1-dbe5-9eba-4ff4 traced four interacting silent-drop paths and confirmed each empirically; this epic closes all four and adds round-trip coverage. ADF format-fidelity (preserving links, mentions, panels) is out of scope and will be addressed by a follow-on epic.

## Success Criteria
- The outbound bridge processes every event added to the tracker branch between cron ticks, including events older than HEAD~1, without replaying full history on cold-start — verified by replaying three back-to-back local STATUS commits across one cron interval and observing all three reach Jira within the next outbound run, AND verified by a cold-start simulation (no checkpoint file present) that seeds at HEAD without dumping prior history into Jira
- Jira-originated tickets imported via the inbound bridge preserve their description text through the plain isinstance fix — verified by creating a Jira issue with a multi-paragraph text description and confirming the local desc field contains the text content
- Locally-authored tickets created by a contributor whose git author email is mapped in BRIDGE_USER_MAP (case-insensitive) land in Jira with the configured Jira accountId as assignee — verified by adding a mapping to the BRIDGE_USER_MAP repo variable JSON, creating a local ticket, and inspecting the resulting Jira issue
- Locally-authored tickets with no user-map entry produce a BRIDGE_ALERT and arrive in Jira explicitly unassigned via a two-step pattern (POST create then PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/assignee with accountId null) — verified by creating a ticket under an unmapped git author and observing the alert plus the unassigned Jira issue
- A round-trip integration test asserts local-CREATE then outbound then mocked Jira REST v3 GET then inbound then local-state preserves description text and assignee identity end-to-end, includes a failure-injection matrix that independently reverts each of the four fixes (cursor, env_id, ADF isinstance, null-assignee) and confirms each revert produces a diagnostic test failure, and includes at least one case driven through the shell/workflow entry point rather than only the Python module boundary
- BRIDGE_ENV_ID is set as a non-empty repository variable, both outbound-bridge.yml and inbound-bridge.yml fail fast (precondition check) when the variable is empty, and filter_bridge_events treats empty bridge_env_id as back-compat pass-through (no filter applied) — verified by inspecting workflow run logs for the precondition check and by unit-testing filter_bridge_events with bridge_env_id empty

## Dependencies
None external. Internal story sequencing: S2 (BRIDGE_ENV_ID hygiene + filter_bridge_events hardening) must land before or with S1 (cursor) — otherwise the cursor will walk past pre-existing events with env_id empty and they will be permanently filtered as bridge-origin echoes. S5 (round-trip test) depends on S1, S2, S3, and S4 being complete so that the test is authored against post-fix code.

## Story Map
- S1 Outbound checkpoint-cursor: persist outbound-checkpoint.json on the tracker branch; git fetch --deepen=50 then escalate to --unshallow only if SHA unreachable; SHA-based diff `git log <last_sha>..HEAD --diff-filter=A`; per-event checkpoint advance on partial Jira push success; cold-start / corruption / unreachable-SHA / ahead-of-HEAD all seed at HEAD plus emit BRIDGE_ALERT; safety cap N=500 commits in window; GH Actions concurrency group bridge-outbound with cancel-in-progress false workflow-level
- S2 BRIDGE_ENV_ID hygiene: set repo variable; fail-loud preconditions in both outbound-bridge.yml and inbound-bridge.yml; harden filter_bridge_events to skip filter when bridge_env_id empty (back-compat); emit one-shot migration BRIDGE_ALERT on first env_id-set transition
- S3 Inbound ADF to text: add _adf_to_text helper; replace isinstance(_raw_desc, str) branch. Plain isinstance fix only — no sidecar, no outbound-skip, no fidelity layer (deferred to follow-on epic)
- S4 User-map mechanism: BRIDGE_USER_MAP repo variable JSON, case-insensitive email lookup; missing-or-empty value then BRIDGE_ALERT + two-step PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/assignee with accountId null; new AcliClient.unassign_issue(jira_key) method (existing _direct_rest_put wraps value field and is wrong shape for this endpoint); empirical verification of ACLI null-assignee wire format with HTTP-trace or fall-back to direct REST v3 call
- S5 Round-trip integration test (depends on S1+S2+S3+S4): mocked Jira v3 GET fixture; failure-injection matrix with 4 independent revert cases (one per fix) each asserting a diagnostic failure; at least one shell-entry-point case

## Linked Bug Tickets
- jira-dig-1995 (P1) — Tickets and their status are not propagating to Jira
- jira-dig-1604 (P1) — Inbound Bridge workflow fails (title is stale; status drift is downstream of S1)
- 92b1-dbe5-9eba-4ff4 (P2) — bridge-outbound assignee Test/Worktree/Claude unassignable, no user-map fallback

SCRUTINY PIPELINE SUMMARY (brainstorm)

Red Team (dso:red-team-reviewer): 11 findings across 7 taxonomy categories.
Blue Team (dso:blue-team-filter): 10 sustained, 1 rejected (per-user ADF deferral).
Plan Review (dso:plan-review): REVISE verdict; feasibility 3, completeness 3, yagni 4, codebase_alignment 3.

All 10 sustained findings folded as expanded done definitions on existing stories per user directive (no scope splits). Major revisions applied:
- BRIDGE_USER_MAP repo variable JSON replaces dso-config.conf (codebase-alignment).
- New AcliClient.unassign_issue() method replaces _direct_rest_put (wrong shape for assignee endpoint).
- S2 must land before or with S1 (filter_bridge_events back-compat dependency).
- Cold-start, corruption, unreachable-SHA all seed at HEAD with BRIDGE_ALERT.
- Bounded fetch (deepen=50, escalate to unshallow only on miss); 500-commit cap.
- Per-event checkpoint advance on partial Jira push success.
- Concurrency group at workflow level (cancel-in-progress false).
- inbound-bridge.yml also gets BRIDGE_ENV_ID precondition.
- BRIDGE_USER_MAP lookup is case-insensitive email; empty value triggers BRIDGE_ALERT + null.
- ACLI null-assignee wire format must be empirically verified or use direct REST v3 fallback.
- S5 includes failure-injection matrix (4 independent reverts, one per fix) and at least one shell-entry-point case.

Investigation provenance: ESCALATED 4-agent fix-bug investigation converged with high confidence and no veto across jira-dig-1995, jira-dig-1604, 92b1-dbe5-9eba-4ff4. Empirical evidence: run 25501576353 HEAD~1..HEAD diff returned only suggestion files; cluster STATUS events at HEAD~4..HEAD~6 invisible.

Unassignment-method research: pycontribs/jira and atlassian-python-api both hardcode accountId null via PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/assignee. Atlassian KB confirms. The -1 sentinel has documented bug JRACLOUD-71153.
